facts.fact: Recombinant DNA technology joins DNA from different sources — the basis of genetic engineering.
Restriction enzymes are 'molecular scissors' that cut DNA at specific sequences.
DNA ligase joins DNA fragments.
Plasmids and bacteriophages act as vectors carrying genes into cells.
PCR amplifies a DNA segment into millions of copies.
CRISPR-Cas9 is a precise gene-editing tool; Charpentier and Doudna won the 2020 Chemistry Nobel.
CRISPR-Cas9 is a bacterial adaptive-immunity system repurposed for editing.
SDN-1 and SDN-2 edits add no foreign DNA; SDN-3 inserts a foreign gene and is treated as GM.
GEAC, under MoEFCC, is the apex regulator for environmental release of GMOs.
GEAC acts under the 1989 Rules made under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986; RCGM (DBT) handles research stages.
Bt cotton (2002) is India's only commercially cultivated GM crop.
Bt brinjal was approved in 2009 but put under a moratorium in 2010.
GM mustard DMH-11 (Delhi University, Deepak Pental) got a GEAC release nod in 2022; the Supreme Court split in 2024.
May 2025: genome-edited rice DRR Dhan 100 (Kamala) and Pusa DST Rice 1 — SDN-1/SDN-2, not transgenic.
Even confined field trials of GM crops need regulatory clearance.
DBT is the nodal biotech department; BIRAC funds biotech start-ups.
BRIC (2024) merged 14 autonomous DBT institutes into one society.
BioE3 Policy (2024) = Biotechnology for Economy, Environment and Employment.
BioE3 promotes high-performance biomanufacturing and biofoundries.
Covaxin (Bharat Biotech + ICMR) is an inactivated-virus vaccine.
ZyCoV-D (Zydus) is the world's first approved human DNA vaccine.
Genome India Project (2020, DBT) sequenced 10,000 Indian genomes for a reference database.
Genome India is coordinated with the IISc Centre for Brain Research.
Covishield is a viral-vector vaccine; Corbevax is a protein-subunit vaccine.
1 nanometre = one-billionth of a metre; properties change at the nanoscale.
India's Nano Mission (2007) is run by the DST.
Graphene is a single layer of carbon atoms in a hexagonal lattice.
Carbon nanotubes have exceptionally high tensile strength.
Quantum dots are semiconductor nanocrystals whose colour depends on size.
Drug delivery = nanomedicine; water membranes = nanotechnology; biofertilisers = agricultural biotech.
The Cartagena Protocol governs safe transboundary movement of living modified organisms.
The Nagoya Protocol covers access to genetic resources and benefit-sharing.
TRIPS (WTO) = Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights.
The Biological Diversity Act, 2002 (amended 2023) checks biopiracy.
AMTZ Visakhapatnam is India's first dedicated medical-devices manufacturing park.
Genome Valley is in the Hyderabad region of Telangana.
Germline editing changes eggs, sperm or embryos, so changes pass to children — a major ethical concern.
DNA barcoding identifies species and food adulterants but cannot tell an organism's age.
The CO1 gene region is the standard animal DNA barcode.
DNA fingerprinting identifies individuals; pioneered in India by Lalji Singh at CCMB Hyderabad.
Mitochondrial DNA comes only from the mother; replacement therapy (three-parent baby) prevents disease.
Bollgard I and II are Bt cotton technologies using Cry genes.
SCNT is used for reproductive cloning — Dolly the sheep (1996).
Recombinant vector vaccines use engineered bacteria or viruses as carriers.
Natural nanoparticles exist (soot, ash); metallic-oxide nanoparticles are used in cosmetics.
Base pairing in DNA: adenine–thymine and guanine–cytosine.
Uracil: base found in RNA in place of thymine.
Rosalind Franklin: X-ray diffraction images that revealed the DNA double helix.
Central dogma: DNA → RNA → protein (Francis Crick).
Codon: three bases that code for one amino acid.
Human Genome Project (1990–2003): about 3 billion base pairs; only about 20,000–25,000 genes.
Human chromosomes: 46 (23 pairs): 22 pairs of autosomes and one pair of sex chromosomes.
Point mutation: change of a single base in DNA.
Epigenetics: changes in gene activity without changing the DNA sequence.
Down syndrome: extra chromosome 21 (trisomy 21).
Klinefelter syndrome: XXY — a male with an extra X chromosome.
Turner syndrome: XO — a female with one X chromosome missing.
Haemophilia: X-linked recessive — blood fails to clot; mostly affects males.
Red-green colour blindness: X-linked recessive — far commoner in males.
Sickle-cell anaemia: autosomal recessive point mutation — glutamic acid replaced by valine in haemoglobin.
Thalassaemia: inherited defect that reduces haemoglobin production.
Phenylketonuria: inborn error — the body cannot break down the amino acid phenylalanine.
National Sickle Cell Anaemia Elimination Mission: launched July 2023 (Shahdol, Madhya Pradesh) — eliminate the disease by 2047.
Casgevy (2023): first approved CRISPR-based medicine — for sickle-cell disease and beta-thalassaemia.
NexCAR19 (2023): India's first indigenous CAR-T cell therapy for blood cancer (IIT Bombay–ImmunoACT).
Recombinant human insulin (Humulin, 1982): first genetically engineered drug — made in E. coli.
First gene therapy (1990): treated ADA (adenosine deaminase) deficiency.
Monoclonal antibodies: identical antibodies from hybridoma cells (Köhler and Milstein, 1975).
ELISA: detects infection by antigen–antibody reaction — immuno-diagnosis (e.g. HIV).
Biosimilar: a near-copy of an approved biological medicine after its patent ends.
Induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSC): adult cells reprogrammed to an embryonic-like state — Shinya Yamanaka (2006, Nobel 2012).
Embryonic vs adult stem cells: embryonic are pluripotent (any cell type); adult are multipotent (limited types).
Cord-blood banking: stores umbilical-cord stem cells for later blood-disorder treatment.
Xenotransplantation: transplanting animal organs (e.g. gene-edited pig kidneys) into humans.
Totipotency: ability of a single plant cell to grow into a whole plant — basis of tissue culture.
Micropropagation: tissue culture that yields thousands of identical plants (somaclones).
Meristem culture: gives virus-free plants (e.g. banana, sugarcane, potato).
Somatic hybridisation: fusing protoplasts of two species — e.g. the "pomato".
Golden rice: engineered to make beta-carotene (provitamin A).
Flavr Savr tomato (1994): first genetically modified food sold.
RNA interference (RNAi): silences a pest gene — nematode-resistant tobacco (Meloidogyne incognita).
Techniques for transgenic crops (UPSC 2014): cytoplasmic male sterility and gene silencing — not budding or grafting.
Bt toxin: Cry protein from the soil bacterium Bacillus thuringiensis, toxic to specific insects.
Biofertilisers: Rhizobium (legume root nodules), Azotobacter, Azospirillum, cyanobacteria (Anabaena, Nostoc), mycorrhiza.
Biopesticides: Bt, the fungus Trichoderma and baculoviruses (NPV).
Oil-eating "superbug": Ananda Chakrabarty's Pseudomonas — first patented living organism (1980).
Bioremediation: using microbes to clean pollutants such as oil spills.
Methanogens: bacteria (e.g. Methanobacterium) that produce methane in biogas plants.
Rosie (1997): transgenic cow whose milk contained human alpha-lactalbumin.
Garima (2009): India's first cloned buffalo — NDRI Karnal.
Noori (2012): world's first cloned Pashmina goat — SKUAST Kashmir.
Dolly (1996): first mammal cloned from an adult body cell — Roslin Institute, Scotland.
Department of Biotechnology (DBT): set up in 1986, separated from the DST.
BIRAC: Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council — public enterprise of DBT, set up 2012.
National Institute of Immunology (NII): New Delhi — immunology and vaccine research.
CCMB (CSIR): Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology, Hyderabad.
CDFD: Centre for DNA Fingerprinting and Diagnostics, Hyderabad.
ICGEB: International Centre for Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology — New Delhi, Trieste and Cape Town.
Rajiv Gandhi Centre for Biotechnology (RGCB): Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala.
IGIB (CSIR): Institute of Genomics and Integrative Biology, New Delhi.
NABI: National Agri-Food Biotechnology Institute, Mohali.
Indian Biological Data Centre (IBDC): Faridabad — India's first national repository for life-science data (2022).
National Biopharma Mission (2017): DBT–BIRAC mission with the World Bank ('Innovate in India', i3) for biopharmaceuticals.
Institute of Nano Science and Technology (INST): Mohali, Punjab — set up under the Nano Mission.
Section 3(d), Patents Act: bars patents on new forms of known medicines without better efficacy (anti-evergreening).
Novartis v. Union of India (2013): Supreme Court refused a patent for the cancer drug Glivec under Section 3(d).
Diamond v. Chakrabarty (1980): US Supreme Court allowed the first patent on a living (GM) organism.
Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers' Rights Act, 2001: protects plant breeders and farmers' rights to save, use and sell seed.
National Biodiversity Authority (2003): Chennai — approves access to biological resources under the Biological Diversity Act.
Assisted Reproductive Technology (Regulation) Act, 2021: regulates IVF clinics and sperm/egg banks.
Surrogacy (Regulation) Act, 2021: bans commercial surrogacy; allows only altruistic surrogacy.
Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD): adopted at the Rio Earth Summit, 1992 — parent of Cartagena and Nagoya.
Cartagena Protocol dates: adopted 2000, in force 2003.
Nagoya Protocol dates: adopted 2010, in force 2014.
Traditional Knowledge Digital Library (TKDL): India's database that blocks patents on traditional remedies (turmeric, neem, basmati cases).
He Jiankui (China, 2018): created the first gene-edited (CRISPR) babies — condemned and jailed.
Richard Feynman (1959): "There's Plenty of Room at the Bottom" — the idea of nanotechnology.
Norio Taniguchi (1974): coined the word "nanotechnology".
Scanning tunnelling microscope (1981): first instrument to image individual atoms (Nobel 1986).
Fullerene C60 ("buckyball", 1985): football-shaped carbon molecule — 1996 Chemistry Nobel.
Carbon nanotubes (1991): described by Sumio Iijima — rolled sheets of graphene.
Graphene (2004): isolated by Andre Geim and Konstantin Novoselov — 2010 Physics Nobel.
Quantum dots: discovery and synthesis won the 2023 Chemistry Nobel (Bawendi, Brus, Ekimov).
Carbon nanotube uses (UPSC 2020): drug and antigen carriers, artificial blood capillaries, biochemical sensors; they are biodegradable.
Top-down vs bottom-up: top-down carves bulk material smaller; bottom-up builds from atoms and molecules.
Nano-silver: antibacterial coating in dressings, textiles and water filters.
Titanium dioxide and zinc oxide nanoparticles: transparent UV blockers in sunscreens and cosmetics.
Lotus effect: nano-rough water-repelling surfaces that clean themselves.
IFFCO Nano Urea (2021): world's first nano-fertiliser; IFFCO Nano DAP followed in 2023.
Nanoparticle risks (UPSC 2013): accumulate in soil and water, enter food chains, trigger free-radical damage.
Live-attenuated: weakened live germ — oral polio, measles, BCG.
Inactivated: killed germ — Covaxin, injectable polio (IPV).
Subunit / recombinant protein: only a piece of the germ — hepatitis B (first recombinant vaccine), Corbevax.
Toxoid: inactivated toxin — tetanus, diphtheria.
Viral vector: harmless carrier virus delivers the germ gene — Covishield, Sputnik V.
mRNA: gives cells instructions to make the antigen — Pfizer, Moderna; India's GEMCOVAC (Gennova).
iNCOVACC (Bharat Biotech, 2022): India's first intranasal (nasal-drop) COVID-19 vaccine.
Cervavac (Serum Institute, 2022): India's first indigenous HPV vaccine against cervical cancer.
Corbevax maker: Biological E, Hyderabad.
